title: Uefa World Cup boycott may be raised over Fifa plan
description: Uefa's 55 member associations will hold an emergency meeting this week to discuss Fifa's controversial proposals to sell stakes in its major competitions.
fullText:
Uefa's 55 member associations will hold an emergency meeting later this week to discuss Fifa's controversial proposals to sell stakes in its major competitions.

Football's world governing body has said it wants to create a new commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including the World Cup, and external investors will be able to buy stakes in it.

That has prompted fears that too much influence in those competitions will be handed to private investors, although Fifa says it will enable more money to be distributed to football associations around the globe.

European football's governing body took the remarkable step of issuing a response to Fifa's plans before they had been published on Tuesday, responding to initial reports in the Financial Times and the Times as it condemned the plans, saying they had "crossed a line".

The meeting will be held virtually and offer the opportunity to work out a plan of action.

Given the strength of feeling – the Football Association says it was not consulted before Fifa released its proposals shortly after Uefa's statement was made public – it would be a surprise if the possibility of a boycott was not at least raised.

While Uefa knows it only accounts for a quarter of Fifa's 211-country membership, the body includes most of the world's most successful teams.

Six of the eight quarter-finalists - and the winners, Spain - at this summer's World Cup were European. In the 2022 and 2018 editions the figures were five and six respectively.

Uefa knows any competition Fifa puts together would be far less valuable if its members were not involved.

Fifa's argument that it is compelled to look at proposals that would help it grow the game globally has led to fears that, in the search for greater revenue, its major competitions - the men's and women's World Cup and corresponding Club World Cup - could be played more often and include more participants.

That would have huge implications for the football calendar, which is already squeezed, partly because of the expansion of European club competitions.

One senior source within the English game told BBC Sport that the threat posed by Fifa's plan is one of the biggest the game has faced and is on a par with the European Super League, which created such controversy in 2021 and was scrapped within 48 hours.

It seems improbable that Fifa will back down in the same manner.

Fifa said its plan is to extend global development funding to $10bn (£7.5bn). It is also planning to offer each of the 211 member associations the opportunity to access up to $20m (£15m) in one-off capital.

This latest escalation extends a difficult relationship between Fifa and Uefa, which responded angrily to attempts to host the World Cup every two years when the idea was floated by former Arsenal manager and Fifa's current chief of global football development Arsene Wenger in 2021.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin boycotted the World Cup final this month in protest at a number of controversial moves.

They included US President Donald Trump stepping in to help turn USA forward Folarin Balogun's one-match ban into a suspended ban, allowing him to play in the last-16 encounter with Belgium.

title: Fifa’s shameful scheme to sell off World Cup is gravest existential threat to football yet - but will anyone stop it?
description: Fifa’s latest money-spinning wheeze, to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investment, has been met with horror. Now its member associations must make a stand against ‘football’s nuclear bomb’
fullText:
Fifa spent 1,403 words in a public statement seeking to rationalise their new plan to sell off stakes of the World Cup to private investment, but a few choice phrases are now ringing out elsewhere.

“Shocking.” “Football’s nuclear bomb.” “Worse than the Super League, and bigger than 115.” “The line in the sand.”

None of that is exaggerated because it ties together so many of the extremes that have been pushing, pulling and twisting football - let alone the world - for so long, potentially crystallising so much of what has been coming to dictate its future: what the game should be and what it’s becoming; how it repeatedly shows it has a social value that you can’t buy as so many involved try to financially exploit that; what people say in private and what gets done in public.

You can even roll that right up to the seemingly dry details of governance like how the people who are going to vote on this - the heads of the member associations - are in many cases directly paid by Fifa through positions and committees.

This is when all of that matters most. How are they going to vote?

And, maybe most pertinently given the direction of the sport for so long, where is the resistance going to come from? Uefa have talked a good game, with a statement that directly says this “crosses a line” and rightly asserts the World Cup’s is “not FIFA’s to sell” - but are they finally going to play a hand?

Is this long-running tension going to spill out into a war that football arguably needs? Is anyone going to look at the bigger picture and actually make a stand?

Because, and this really can’t be stressed enough, once you start selling the game off, there’s really no getting it back.

Typical of how football and the world are going, Fifa’s 1,403-word statement of course turned all of this rationale on its head. It’s of a piece with Gianni Infantino’s unhinged Sunday statement about criticism. This announcement was headlined “Fifa intends to expand football development funding to over USD 10 billion subject to approval by FIFA Member Associations”, so duly framed by ideas of redistribution and democracy.

Once again, a not-for-profit raising money, any money, was automatically elevated as if it’s a good thing without any further thought. The core reality was finally referenced a bit further down, as Fifa spoke of “carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests” in the new Fifa Forward Enterprise programme. That is set to bring the creation of a new company being formed to run the primary competitions, where Fifa would own a majority stake, private investors would have 20-30% and then the 211 members a small stake totalling around 20%.

Except, “non-controlling” isn’t how such money tends to really work. In reality, that kind of money brings a lot of influence.

There are profound concerns here even beyond the core philosophical virtue that the World Cup only belongs to the countries of the world - and, by extension, its football communities - and that’s it. What do they think happens once you allow such interests in? There might be the short-term benefit of being able to point your own national association to newly flush cash reserves of up to $20m - but what next?

Clue: such interests don’t tend to have wider societal concerns; they don’t care for what doesn’t make money. As one source puts it, “the current stakeholders benefit but everyone loses out in the future”. Trickle-down economics don’t work here, as the last few decades of football have made emphatically clear. This is why Celtic or Ajax don’t win the Champions League any more. It’s why every other country suffers a talent drain to western Europe.

And what would now be directly incentivised - especially through the establishment of a company to run all of this - is the expansion of the Club World Cup and all of the ideas that serve existing wealth, both in the game and society. It shouldn’t be forgotten that Infantino was involved in Super League discussions, with the clubs at one point thinking they had Fifa’s blessing.

The global governing body have now already confirmed that Josh Kushner - brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner - has been in talks about becoming the proposed lead investor.

Infantino’s long relationship with the US president suddenly takes on an even sharper perspective, especially among the mooted next steps for this. An excellent exclusive by Martyn Ziegler of the Times has already broached that Infantino would be lined up to run the company as a “commissioner” once his final presidential term expires in 2031. In other words, a lucrative post-presidency life.

When you stand back, this looks a lot like one man using his position - and the sport - for personal betterment. Or, as one senior insider put it, “only in Infantino’s world can things somehow get worse for the game every day”.

It should be what anyone who cares for the sport stands against, but will those with actual say really do that? Will they, as one other insider states, “put their bollocks on the line”?

Some who despise the idea have already marvelled at its realpolitik “genius”, likening it to the fait accompli of the Saudi Arabia 2034 “acclamation” in how everything already looks lined up. Every individual association would get a huge figure - or could sell off some of their share in the new company - so those in power right now are clearly incentivised to vote for it. And this in a world where only a fifth of member associations actually return audited accounts to show how the money is used.

It reminds us how broken the system is, how the reform that was supposed to take place after Infantino succeeded Sepp Blatter never happened. And in that structure, how is this actually going to be stopped when such a financially attractive package is taken to Congress for approval and there are no checks and balances?

It all speaks to this central long-running theme of the game being taken further and further away from those who have an actual emotional stake in it; a personal stake - right up to the ownership of clubs. Members of the Fifa Council insisted they only found out through the media, re-iterating how the body now works. The FA, chaired by Fifa vice-president Debbie Hewitt, were completely unaware of the proposal and it was not mentioned at Friday’s board meeting.

Many similar figures declared themselves shocked, appalled, disgusted. Except we’ve heard so much of this before. This, more than ever before, is a time to act. Could Uefa countries actually threaten to pull out… or will the individual countries just look at those financial figures?

The world should watch how everyone votes on this. Hiding behind the majority, and pointing to Fifa’s dismally dull politics, will no longer cut it. This is a decision with repercussions way beyond all of that.

This is what all of the politics, all the game’s long problems, were ultimately leading to. This is the line.

title: Uefa says Fifa plan for private investment in World Cup 'crosses line'
description: European football's governing body Uefa reacts furiously to proposals from Fifa to seek private investment in its competitions, including the World Cup.
fullText:
European football's governing body Uefa has reacted furiously to proposals from Fifa to seek private investment in its competitions, including the World Cup.

Fifa - the sport's global governing body - said it intends to expand "football development funding" to more than $10bn (£7.5bn) and invite third-party investment in a new venture.

The story was first reported in the Financial Times and the Times, with the latter claiming the plans could potentially earn Fifa president Gianni Infantino tens of millions of pounds.

In a lengthy statement outlining the proposals, Fifa says it will "invite third parties to make minority, non-controlling investments" in a new subsidiary - Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) - to "consolidate" its commercial and event operations.

The plan still needs to be passed by a vote of Fifa's 211 member nations. But if approval is granted, Fifa says Thrive Eternal is expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE.

Thrive is an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared.

Fifa sources have told BBC Sport there has been no discussion over Infantino, or anyone else, becoming chief executive of FFE.

In its statement, Fifa did say Infantino and the rest of the organisation "has a duty" to control the development of the project. Fifa has not said precisely what that means, or what the specific nature of Infantino's involvement will be.

As part of its pitch Fifa says all member associations will be able to access up to $20m (£15m) in "one-off capital" to fund development.

Infantino said every nation should benefit from the riches football creates.

"Parts of the game have turned that popularity into remarkable commercial value - and we celebrate that success and want it to continue, because it lifts the whole game," he said.

"Our job is to make sure the rest of football grows with it: Fifa exists to support sustainable, inclusive development in every corner of the world."

However, Uefa has issued a statement criticising the proposals, which it claimed "crosses a line".

The Football Association says it was unaware of Fifa's plans when they were released.

Fifa argues its plan, with a dedicated commercial subsidiary, is similar to that used by governing bodies in other sports.

In 2018, Premiership Rugby announced a partnership with private equity and investment advisory firm CVC Capital Partners.

However, Uefa sees Tuesday's announcement as a step too far - and raises the potential for further expansion of Fifa competitions in order to raise revenue, both in terms of size and frequency, which could threaten its own lucrative competitions.

"This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross," Uefa said.

"Uefa takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder who cares about the future of the game.

"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not Fifa's to sell."

Fifa says it would retain control of FFE "and exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, the international match calendar and all regulatory and sporting decisions".

The matter is likely to be a topic of conversation at the next Fifa Council meeting in the autumn and then around the Fifa Intercontinental Cup, featuring Champions League winners Paris St-Germain, in December.

The proposal could be voted on by all 211 members at the Fifa Congress in Morocco in March.

Quite aside from the unease many will feel at the potential involvement of private equity investors - and someone with close ties to Donald Trump - being at the centre of this, there is also a fight being played out for control of the game.

Fifa's stated aim of developing the sport worldwide is unsettling for those closer to home.

One senior English football executive told BBC Sport privately that today's announcement was the biggest story since the European Super League plan - and raised just as many concerns.

The issue is if there is a drive to generate more finance through Fifa competitions, that will mean expansion - both in the number of teams and the frequency of both the World Cup and the Club World Cup.

Some also feel the scale of the tournaments will be such they may end up being played in the winter months.

That would put more pressure on the calendar, which is already being squeezed at domestic level, partly because of the expansion of European competition.

And the basic reality is that while $20m is not a significant sum in the English game, for many countries globally, it is huge - and will be supported.

However, it still remains to be seen what the respective stakeholders - associations, leagues, clubs and players - make of the plan.

fullText:
Manchester City defender Josko Gvardiol has officially signed a new five-year contract to extend his stay at Etihad Stadium.

The 24-year-old, who joined the club from RB Leipzig in August 2023, has since made 122 appearances and won six trophies under previous manager Pep Guardiola.

Gvardiol contributed two goals and five assists across 25 appearances last season, while also representing Croatia at his second World Cup this summer.

He also played a pivotal role as Manchester City became the first team in English football to secure four consecutive top-flight titles in 2023-24.

"As soon as I knew City wanted to renew my contract, I felt straight away that it was what I wanted," Gvardiol said. "The fans have been unbelievable with me from day one and the club provides absolutely everything for its players.

"It is the best club in the world to be at. I have felt so much love and respect during my three years here, and I don't take that for granted.

"The players we have here are amazing. This is a world-class squad that is young and full of potential.

"I truly believe we will have a lot of success in the coming years."

Director of football Hugo Viana added: "He epitomises what we want in our defenders. He can play in multiple positions, he is quick and strong, and when he attacks he does it superbly.

"He is exceptional, but the way he conducts himself is also very impressive. This young man is determined to be the best he can be - an approach totally aligned with our overall vision."

title: MLS make Lionel Messi exception over punishment rule that left him ‘very upset’ in 2025
description: The MLS have decided to exempt Lionel Messi from the huge punishment that they imposed on him in 2025. With the FIFA World Cup ending just a little over a week ago, many have wondered when Lionel Messi would return to Inter Miami.
fullText:
The MLS have decided to exempt Lionel Messi from the huge punishment that they imposed on him in 2025.

With the FIFA World Cup ending just a little over a week ago, many have wondered when Lionel Messi would return to Inter Miami.

Messi helped lead Argentina to the FIFA World Cup final and has been away from his club side since then as he recovers, which will force him to miss one of the MLS’s landmark events.

Lionel Messi is confirmed to be missing the 2026 MLS All-Star week in Charlotte, North Carolina, as he takes time away from Inter Miami following a grueling FIFA World Cup.

MLS officials confirmed to ESPN that Messi will not receive a one-match suspension for missing the festivities, the standard punishment issued to players.

However, this isn’t a case of Messi receiving preferential treatment as a star player, as the MLS had agreed to let players participating in the FIFA World Cup get some time off to recover.

This is why Messi and Rodrigo de Paul are exempt from the punishment, as a statement from the MLS revealed:

“Prior to the start of the 2026 season, Major League Soccer and the MLS Players Association agreed that upon a player’s exit from the World Cup competition, clubs would have individual conversations with each player to determine the appropriate rest and return to training and competition timeline.

“Consistent with that agreement, Rodrigo De Paul and Lionel Messi will be excused from participating in the 2026 MLS All-Star Game.”

This decision is a stark contrast to last year, when Messi, along with Jordi Alba, received a one-match suspension for missing the event.

This decision was criticized by Miami Heat co-owner Jorge Mas last year, who revealed how upset Messi was over the ‘draconian’ punishment.

“Lionel Messi is very upset, like we all are in the club, with the fact that they won’t be able to play tomorrow night.

“But I think what we have to do as a club is to get together as one, have an attitude that is us against the world… I think that the punishment for the rule is frankly draconian.

“Obviously, it was not a positive reaction [from Messi and Alba]. They want to compete, they want to play games.

“That’s what they’re here for, to play and win. They understand the magnitude of tomorrow night’s game.

“So no, their reaction was exactly as expected of two competitive players who don’t understand the decision, who don’t understand why not attending an exhibition match leads directly to a suspension.”

title: Meditate, pray or watch football instead of spreading hate - Infantino
description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino tells critics to "meditate, pray or watch a football match" instead of "spreading hate and false rumours" about him and the World Cup.
fullText:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino has told critics to "meditate, pray or watch a football match" instead of "spreading hate and false rumours" about his leadership, the governing body and the World Cup.

In a 15-slide post on his personal Instagram account - reposted to Fifa's eight million followers - Infantino addressed "those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens" to affirm his belief that, while they were "busy planting seeds of hate", Fifa was delivering the "greatest event on earth".

He said the World Cup "celebrated humanity at its best", adding that the 2026 tournament had "100% safety and security, only joy and happiness".

Infantino downplayed several of the tournament's high-profile controversies and hailed the involvement of Iran, who featured at the World Cup despite their ongoing conflict with co-hosts the United States, as a success.

He said Fifa "worked tirelessly to unite two countries at war", with Iran entering the country "without incident or conflict".

His comments are in stark contradiction to those of Iran's head coach Amir Ghalenoei, who said his team were the "most oppressed" at the World Cup.

Infantino's 'time is up' with Fifa - La Liga boss

The country that doesn't play football... yet

Iran faced visa delays, "integral" members of their backroom staff were denied entry to the US and fans had their allocation of tickets revoked, while Iran also had to move their training base from Tucson, Arizona to Tijuana, Mexico following a multitude of logistical issues in the build up to the tournament.

They later also encountered restrictions on their movements as they travelled between their training base and group matches in Los Angeles and Seattle.

Such issues were not unique to Iran, with fans from Haiti, Senegal, and Ivory Coast impacted by travel bans imposed by the Trump administration, while Somali referee Omar Artan was denied entry to the US - despite holding a diplomatic passport and a single entry US visa - because of his "association with suspected members of terror organisations".

Infantino wrote: "You mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world. Because football unites the world, and it was impressively demonstrated this summer."

Doubling down on the tournament's safety, Infantino said there were "zero incidents, zero violence, just joy, emotions, happiness, unity, and togetherness".

However, Fifa is investigating Argentina's actions after players and backroom staff were involved in altercations with Spain's players after losing the World Cup final. It is also investigating allegations of racist abuse towards American social media influencer IShowSpeed, while supporters were arrested at multiple matches - including following England's semi-final against Argentina in Atlanta.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials were also controversially present at World Cup stadiums.

Infantino also addressed criticism surrounding the standard of officiating at the tournament, in particular concerns about political interference after USA forward Folarin Balogun was made available for their last-16 tie when his one-match ban was suspended by Fifa - following the intervention of US President Donald Trump.

Of the 191 other red cards shown at a men's World Cup, only one other player has escaped a suspension.

Uefa said the decision had "crossed a red line", labelling it "unprecedented, incomprehensible, and unjustifiable", while the Norwegian Football Federation is considering filing a formal complaint to Fifa's ethics committee.

Infantino, however, argued that such decisions are not out of the ordinary, claiming similar rulings are "routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide".

He added: "It's curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising."

The International Olympic Committee has said it will not investigate Infantino for any possible breaches of political neutrality, stating the complaint levelled by human rights campaign group FairSquare falls outside the jurisdiction of its ethics commission.

Infantino's advice to his opponents was "to show some love" and "respect" to a tournament where "people came together as families, as fans, as one".

"To everyone who missed our beautiful game, the emotions, the celebrations, the laughter, the crying, the deception and the joy. To all of you who missed watching kids, babies, grandparents and parents come together for the beautiful game... sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all," Infantino wrote.

"While they celebrated, you were busy planting seeds of hate. Our world needs love, not hate; tolerance, not division; celebration, not mourning.

"To those spending their time and energy hating us, please take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray or watch a football match and truly observe the faces, the eyes, the emotions.

"Because only our beautiful game can deliver such an extraordinary show, a show where everyone becomes one and reconnects as humans.

"I am incredibly proud, as Fifa President, to have contributed, even a little, to this show. It's a great feeling."

It may be that Infantino's astonishing outburst reflects a genuine grievance he feels about some of the criticism Fifa has faced over its handling of the World Cup. It appears he does not believe the governing body has received enough credit for organising a tournament that enjoyed record ticket sales, entertained many millions, and successfully delivered a huge security operation, despite the tense geopolitical landscape. It also arguably conveys a high degree of confidence in his position and chances of re-election next year, that he feels he can be so defiant.

But for many, turning on his critics in such a fashion, and portraying them as negative, biased and unfair 'haters', risks reinforcing an impression that Fifa is unable or unwilling to handle legitimate scrutiny, and is out of touch.

The reality is that a host of controversies made such scrutiny inevitable; the issues related to US visa policies, which undermined claims that it would be the most welcoming tournament ever. The unprecedented costs facing fans. The outcry over Fifa's suspension of Folarin Balogun's ban after lobbying by US President Trump, leading to concerns over political interference (regardless of Fifa's denials). The introduction of innovations such as hydration breaks and a 27 minute long half-time show for the final. And the environmental impact of the biggest and longest World Cup ever.

Infantino held a media conference on the eve of the tournament - his first for three years - when he told his critics to "chill & relax". Maybe, if he had conducted another one after the event began or once it ended, he could have addressed some of the issues it raised sooner, and not responded in a way that many will see as further evidence of a siege mentality.

title: Gianni Infantino Lashes Out at World Cup Critics
description: The FIFA president ripped the media in an Instagram post.
fullText:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino posted a 15-slide message directed at people “busy planting seeds of hate” on Instagram on Sunday night, claiming the World Cup went off without incident.

Infantino’s Sunday night missive began: “To everyone who missed our beautiful game…sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all.” He went on to further single out people “behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours.”

The post was filled with jarring and inaccurate claims; he wrote that the World Cup saw “zero incidents, zero hostility, zero violence, just joy, emotions, happiness, unity, and togetherness.”

Four people died during celebrations in Mexico City after Mexico beat Ecuador in the round of 32. South African midfielder Jayden Adams was found dead in Cape Town after returning from the tournament, and police are investigating a cause of death.

FIFA did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the inaccuracies or what prompted Infantino’s post.

Even and especially at its best, the World Cup—as always—stirred up hostility and political tensions. Argentine fans in Atlanta were captured on video fighting with one another on the night before the match, and with England fans after the semifinal win. The match reignited historic claims from the Argentine government, players, and fans against Great Britain over the Falkland Islands, including with an on-pitch demonstration by the players. In the U.K., more domestic abuse incidents were reported during the tournament than the past two World Cups and Euros.

Infantino also wrote that “Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict.” Iran’s coach, though, said his side was “perhaps the most oppressed” team in the tournament after the quick trip from Tijuana to Los Angeles took five hours with security screenings, then the team would need to return immediately after the match. Iran saw 11 federation members and team staffers denied entry into the U.S., including federation president Mehdi Taj.

The Iranian federation also said it would file a complaint to FIFA for denying its request to travel two days in advance of its match against Belgium.

Infantino wrote that “Football is bigger than hate and discrimination.” Multiple incidents of racist abuse occurred during the World Cup. Most notably, a Paraguayan senator called Kylian Mbappé a “colonised Cameroonian,” to which the French captain called her “a despicable woman and unworthy of your position.”

Infantino said the World Cup’s haters “mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world.”

The most high profile visa cases include that of Somali referee Omar Artan, denied entry into the U.S. over alleged “association with suspected members of terrorist organizations,” and Ghana midfielder Thomas Partey, who was not allowed into Canada for matches due to ongoing rape charges.

And fans from Haiti, Iran, Senegal, and Ivory Coast were simply banned from entering the United States under blanket Trump administration policy; others were subject to a $15,000 bond that deterred many from coming. (FIFA celebrated that it got the U.S. to waive this requirement, but that only applied to a certain subset of fans who had already purchased tickets and opted into an expedited visa process.)

Infantino did not mention Folarin Balogun’s red card or its subsequent suspension directly, but he was still defensive about the notorious incident.

“Indeed, ‘arguable’ referees’ decisions or ‘strange’ disciplinary rulings such as for instance potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide,” Infantino wrote. “It’s curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising.”

European leaders had blasted FIFA’s handlingof Balogun’s red card to the point where UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin—whose organization called the red card reversal an “unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable decision”—boycotted the tournament final. (Some European leagues do review red cards after games, which is not generally FIFA protocol.)

Infantino has not taken questions from reporters since a press conference before the opening match in Mexico City on June 10.

There, Infantino was also defensive and vague, saying, “We try to do our best” on a number of issues like Iran, high ticket prices, and visa restrictions. After initially telling people to “chill, relax,” Infantino later clarified that he meant “to trust us that we are working behind the scenes.”

He was more aggressive on Sunday night.

“To those spending their time and energy hating us, please take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match and truly observe the faces, the eyes, the emotions,” Infantino wrote. “To the pens and papers, to all the screens, may you find love and peace where the people behind you couldn’t.

“May you find peace; we at FIFA have found ours and we deliver it, by delivering the most outstanding FIFA World Cup.”

Also on Sunday night, Rep. Jamie Raskin (D., MD) sent Infantino a letter asking for a list of any money or gifts exchanged between FIFA and anyone related to President Trump, and visitor logs at the governing body’s Miami and New York offices. FIFA houses its New York office in Trump Tower. The Athletic first reported news of the letter.

Raskin also asked Infantino to appear before the House Judiciary Committee, of which he is the ranking member.

title: World Cup 2026: Gianni Infantino slams critics who were 'spreading hate' during event
description: Gianni Infantino decided to celebrate the 2026 World Cup by ... going after its haters.
fullText:
The 2026 World Cup is over, and instead of focusing on the joys of the event, FIFA President Gianni Infantino took a moment to call out its critics in one of his first comments since the final.

In a lengthy social-media post, Infantino ripped critics who he accused of “spreading hate” during the 2026 World Cup.

Infantino’s statement immediately begins with him calling out those who “missed our beautiful game.”

“To all of you who missed watching kids, babies, grandparents, and parents come together for the beautiful game, I say sorry that the matches are now over and sorry that you missed all that joy and togetherness.

“Sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all.”

From there, Infantino appeared to take a shot at journalists covering the 2026 World Cup:

“To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering the best show in the world.

“While you hide, we are exploring the streets of Canada, Mexico, and the United States, talking with fans, engaging with people, and ensuring everyone’s safety.

Infantino then went on to thank the host countries for providing a welcoming atmosphere during games before once again condemning critics of the event.

“While they celebrated, you were busy planting seeds of hate.

“Our world needs love, not hate; tolerance, not division; celebration, not mourning.

“While you spread hatred, we worked tirelessly to unite two countries at war.

“Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict.”

“Football is about unity, not division.

Football is bigger than hate and discrimination.”

In the post, Infantino also addressed “‘arguable’ referees’ decisions.”

“Indeed, ‘arguable’ referees’ decisions or ‘strange’ disciplinary rulings such as for instance potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide.

“It’s curious that the same countries employing these practices are the onces criticising.”

He then ended the statement with, “Much love to all.”

Infantino’s post is … a curious way to address what, on many levels, was a successful World Cup. While the event was subject to plenty of criticism, some due to President Donald Trump’s involvement and the United States’ immigration policies, some due to potential mishandling of punishments handed out during games, particularly one involving USMNT striker Folarin Balogun, there was a lot to celebrate from the actual event.

Videos of opposing fans being embraced and celebrated by United States citizens were among the best part of the 2026 World Cup. When the games actually began, a record number of fans from the U.S. tuned in.

That should have given Infantino plenty to celebrate. Instead, he — for whatever reason — decided to focus on all the potential negatives surrounding the event.

title: Robertson receives first Scotland call-up as Ihsan & Jones return
description: Lyle Robertson receives a first senior Scotland call-up for August's ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 series against Canada and the United Arab Emirates.
fullText:
Lyle Robertson has received a first senior Scotland call-up for August's ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 series against Canada and the United Arab Emirates.

Falkland's Robertson is one of three changes to the squad that toured Nepal in May, with Zainullah Ihsan and Michael Jones also returning.

Meanwhile, Michael Leask drops out, while the injured duo of Brad Currie and Owen Gould are unavailable.

"It's great to welcome back Zainullah Ihsan and Michael Jones to the squad for this series," said Scotland head coach Owen Dawkins.

"Zainullah has shown excellent progress across the summer with his performances in training, in club cricket for GHK and in regional cricket with Western Warriors.

"Michael missed our previous two tours due to his Lancashire commitments, so it's exciting to have a player of his quality available again for a home series.

"We're also pleased to award a first senior international call-up to Lyle Robertson. As a young player he represented Scotland at the ICC Under-19 World Cup in the Caribbean and since then he's continued to show steady development."

The upcoming series will be Scotland's final CWCL2 fixtures, taking place at Forthill in Broughty Ferry.

The Scots currently sit second in the table, alongside the Netherlands, and are five points behind leaders United States.

description: ITV will show next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia, extending the broadcaster's coverage of the tournament to a 10th successive edition.
fullText:
ITV will show next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia, extending the broadcaster's coverage of the tournament to a 10th successive edition.

All 52 matches from the event, which features 24 teams and a last-16 knockout round, will be shown live.

"This is much more than a new agreement with a trusted partner, it is a statement of intent to ensure that everyone in the UK can experience and be inspired by one of the world's iconic sporting events, its action, drama and personalities," said World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin.

The broadcaster, a rights holder for every men's World Cup since the 1991 edition, has previously secured the 2026 and 2028 editions of the new Nations Championship, and the majority of Six Nations fixtures up to and including the 2029 tournament in a shared-rights deal with BBC Sport.

ITV will show every England men's game currently scheduled until summer 2029, while Scotland, Wales and Ireland's matches will also be free-to-air in the United Kingdom over the same period.

The Rugby World Cup opens with hosts Australia taking on Hong Kong on 1 October next year.

title: Infantino tells Fifa critics to 'meditate, pray or watch football'
description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino tells critics to "meditate, pray or watch a football match" instead of "spreading hate and false rumours" about him and the World Cup.
fullText:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino has told critics to "meditate, pray or watch a football match" instead of "spreading hate and false rumours" about his leadership, the governing body and the World Cup.

In a 15-slide post on his personal Instagram account - reposted to Fifa's eight million followers - Infantino addressed "those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens" to affirm his belief that, while they were "busy planting seeds of hate", Fifa was delivering the "greatest event on earth".

He said the World Cup "celebrated humanity at its best", adding that the 2026 tournament had "100% safety and security, only joy and happiness".

Infantino downplayed several of the tournament's high-profile controversies and hailed the involvement of Iran, who featured at the World Cup despite their ongoing conflict with co-hosts the United States, as a success.

He said Fifa "worked tirelessly to unite two countries at war", with Iran entering the country "without incident or conflict".

His comments are in stark contradiction to those of Iran's head coach Amir Ghalenoei, who said his team were the "most oppressed" at the World Cup.

Infantino's 'time is up' with Fifa - La Liga boss

The country that doesn't play football... yet

Iran faced visa delays, "integral" members of their backroom staff were denied entry to the US and fans had their allocation of tickets revoked, while Iran also had to move their training base from Tucson, Arizona to Tijuana, Mexico following a multitude of logistical issues in the build up to the tournament.

They later also encountered restrictions on their movements as they travelled between their training base and group matches in Los Angeles and Seattle.

Such issues were not unique to Iran, with fans from Haiti, Senegal, and Ivory Coast impacted by travel bans imposed by the Trump administration, while Somali referee Omar Artan was denied entry to the US - despite holding a diplomatic passport and a single entry US visa - because of his "association with suspected members of terror organisations".

Infantino wrote: "You mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world. Because football unites the world, and it was impressively demonstrated this summer."

Doubling down on the tournament's safety, Infantino said there were "zero incidents, zero violence, just joy, emotions, happiness, unity, and togetherness".

However, Fifa is investigating Argentina's actions after players and backroom staff were involved in altercations with Spain's players after losing the World Cup final. It is also investigating allegations of racist abuse towards American social media influencer IShowSpeed, while supporters were arrested at multiple matches - including following England's semi-final against Argentina in Atlanta.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials were also controversially present at World Cup stadiums.

Infantino also addressed criticism surrounding the standard of officiating at the tournament, in particular concerns about political interference after USA forward Folarin Balogun was made available for their last-16 tie when his one-match ban was suspended by Fifa - following the intervention of US President Donald Trump.

Of the 191 other red cards shown at a men's World Cup, only one other player has escaped a suspension.

Uefa said the decision had "crossed a red line", labelling it "unprecedented, incomprehensible, and unjustifiable", while the Norwegian Football Federation is considering filing a formal complaint to Fifa's ethics committee.

Infantino, however, argued that such decisions are not out of the ordinary, claiming similar rulings are "routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide".

He added: "It's curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising."

The International Olympic Committee has said it will not investigate Infantino for any possible breaches of political neutrality, stating the complaint levelled by human rights campaign group FairSquare falls outside the jurisdiction of its ethics commission.

Infantino's advice to his opponents was "to show some love" and "respect" to a tournament where "people came together as families, as fans, as one".

"To everyone who missed our beautiful game, the emotions, the celebrations, the laughter, the crying, the deception and the joy. To all of you who missed watching kids, babies, grandparents and parents come together for the beautiful game... sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all," Infantino wrote.

"While they celebrated, you were busy planting seeds of hate. Our world needs love, not hate; tolerance, not division; celebration, not mourning.

"To those spending their time and energy hating us, please take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray or watch a football match and truly observe the faces, the eyes, the emotions.

"Because only our beautiful game can deliver such an extraordinary show, a show where everyone becomes one and reconnects as humans.

"I am incredibly proud, as Fifa President, to have contributed, even a little, to this show. It's a great feeling."

title: 9️⃣ players to watch as the 2026 MLS Season returns
description: The 2026 World Cup is over, and we bring our attention back to Major League Soccer as we kick off the second half of the season. Here are some of the stars and breakout candidates who could shape the ...
fullText:
The 2026 World Cup is over, and we bring our attention back to Major League Soccer as we kick off the second half of the season.

Here are some of the stars and breakout candidates who could shape the second half of the season.

Inter Miami vs. Columbus on August 1 at 7:30pm ET. Watch live on Apple TV

New York Red Bull vs. Orlando City on August 1 at 7:30pm ET. Watch live on Apple TV

Chicago vs. Charlotte on August 1 at 8:30pm ET. Watch live on Apple TV

📸 Charlotte Wilson - 2026 Getty Images

One of the breakout stars in the West was tipped to perform highly at the World Cup, and with his former USMNT head coach-for-a-father watching, he did!

Midfielder Sebastian Berhalter impressed under Mauricio Pochettino, notably featuring in all five World Cup games and registering a goal plus an assist against Turkiye. That made him the first American in the modern era to record one goal and one assist in a World Cup match.

He already has 10 combined goals and assists in 14 MLS appearances this season, something he'll look to build on after gaining some confidence seeing his stock rise.

One of the biggest stories following the resumption of the MLS season is Inter Miami's signing of Casemiro. The five-time Champions League winner arrives in South Florida as another marquee addition to a star-studded squad, with hopes of helping Miami strengthen their push for MLS Cup.

The Brazilian could well make his debut this weekend after completing his move late last week, bringing a wealth of experience and winning mentality to Nu Stadium.

Casemiro made more than 120 appearances for Manchester United, winning the Carabao Cup and FA Cup during his time at Old Trafford. While his impact won't be measured in goals, his ability to control games, break up attacks and lead by example could prove just as valuable as Miami chase more silverware.

One of the biggest headlines as we return to the MLS season was Chicago's signing of Robert Lewandowski from Barcelona. The 37-year-old is the latest to come to America as a blockbuster transfer, hoping to help the Fire rise from third to first.

Lewandowski was denied a debut against Thomas Müller's Whitecaps due to smoky weather conditions, so it remains to be seen how he will kick off this new chapter.

He scored 14 goals from 31 appearances for the Blaugrana last season and walked away with a stunning record of 120 in 193. Though it's not really about how many he'll score for Chicago, rather, it's when. Everyone will be on high alert to watch his first hit the back of the net.

One of the youngsters who impressed in the first half of the season was Kevin Kelsy of the Portland Timbers. And he's already back up and running after the restart!

At just 21 years old, the Venezuelan centre-forward is impressing at the club, having scored 26% of their overall goals this season. He netted twice against Seattle Sounders, the first a looping header and the second a quick reaction to poke the ball home after crashing the box.

The brace sees him lead Portland's scoring charts this season, and after impressing against a rival, we're sure he will be flowing with confidence in the second half showing.

📸 Shaun Botterill - 2026 Getty Images

Naturally, how can we not mention Lionel Messi? The Argentina captain went all the way to the 2026 World Cup final while staying in contention for the Golden Boot. His ever-reliable presence for the national team is something we expect to continue for Inter Miami.

The Herons sit in second place in the Eastern Conference, largely thanks to Messi's brilliance. He already has 12 goals and seven assists after only 14 appearances this season.

That said, it will be interesting to see whether the 39-year-old experiences any fatigue as he re-enters the regular season. World Cup players are often given deserved breaks, and if Miami allows Messi to take a temporary vacation, who will step up in his absence? Without his impact, will the Herons struggle to fight for first?

A second headline signing heading into the back half of the season is Antoine Griezmann joining Orlando City. The Frenchman arrives in the United States after an impressive final season in Spain, where he registered 14 goals and eight assists across all competitions.

The Lions will look to the 35-year-old's storied experience to help lift them up from 13th in the table after just four wins so far. That poor form sees the club sit third last in the Eastern Conference.

That said, Griezmann has said he's prepared to be a leader for Orlando. "I want to win the championship, score goals, provide assists, encourage kids to play football and make them Orlando City fans," he said. "I came for all of this: I want to take Orlando City to the top of football in the United States."

📸 Dustin Satloff - 2026 Getty Images

Another youngster with his name in lights during the first half of the season was Julian Hall of the New York Red Bulls. And he's perhaps the most talked-about teenager currently in MLS.

The 18-year-old has a stunning 13 goal contributions (nine goals and four assists) from just 15 appearances. Add to that, there are also three other goals from two U.S Open Cup showings. Such numbers look like that of a veteran centre forward, rather than a high-school graduate.

After feeling refreshed from the break, it's time to see whether or not he will continue generating such hype.

After an early World Cup exit, Son Heung-min appears to be back and ready to put his best foot forward with LAFC.

The 34-year-old was a staple creative presence for the club prior to the international break, registering nine assists to help them sit third in West. That includes a statement showing against Orlando, where he produced five alone!

Now, however, Son appears hungry for goals. He scored his first of the season during the first game back against rivals LA Galaxy. Perhaps an early elimination from the World Cup and some rest was just what he needed?

📸 Alex Slitz - 2026 Getty Images

After an impressive run to the Round of 16 with Canada, defender Richie Laryea will be a player with the weight of BMO Field on his shoulders.

The veteran right-back demonstrated his veteran persona at the World Cup by playing a full 90 minutes in almost every one of Canada's games. A five-game starter, the earliest he was ever substituted off was the 78th minute.

TFC's injury issues before the break have left them struggling in 12th place in the East, but Laryea is the voice and presence at the back who can guide the team up the standings if and when he's at his best.

Looking at his stats, he has 15 goals and 26 assists in 155 appearances across all competitions for the club. He was also selected as an MLS All-Star. Will the hometown talent rise to the occasion in the second half of the season?

title: Eric Garcia reflects on Spain World Cup win: ‘No coincidence that Ferran scored the World Cup winner’
description: Eric Garcia has revealed that his next major ambition is to win the UEFA Champions League with Barcelona after helping Spain lift the FIFA World Cup.The 25-year-old defender, one of eight Barcelona pl...
fullText:
Eric Garcia has revealed that his next major ambition is to win the UEFA Champions League with Barcelona after helping Spain lift the FIFA World Cup.

The 25-year-old defender, one of eight Barcelona players in Spain’s victorious squad, is currently enjoying a well-earned break before returning for the new season.

Speaking to COPE (h/t Mundo Deportivo), Garcia reflected on the World Cup triumph, praised teammate Ferran Torres and looked ahead to his objectives with Barcelona.

Garcia admitted he was deeply moved by the reception the squad received during the victory celebrations and reserved special praise for Ferran Torres, whose goal secured Spain’s World Cup title.

Asked about the sports psychologist he shares with the Barcelona forward, Garcia highlighted the mental work both players have put in throughout their careers.

Spain’s hero. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images)

“For better or for worse, and I can include myself in that, both Ferran and I are used to surprises. Our job is to play football, which I think is a privilege,” he said.

“Things, as I’ve always said, can go better, they can go worse, but you always have to be there, with the right attitude. And in the end, it’s no coincidence that he scored the goal that gave us the World Cup.”

Garcia also reflected on making his World Cup debut in the tournament’s biggest match, explaining that he had remained prepared throughout the competition despite not featuring earlier.

“I’d been preparing all month in case the opportunity arose, and look, it finally came in the final. And to win it, which was everyone’s goal. We were all there to contribute, whether we played or not,” the Barcelona defender said.

“I’d always told the manager I was ready for whatever came my way,” he added.

Champions League the next goal. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

The defender also revealed the moment Spain began to believe the trophy was within reach, saying:

“After Enzo’s sending-off and when they took Julian off and brought on another defender.”

Having added the World Cup to an already impressive list of honours, Garcia made it clear that his focus has now shifted to European success with Barcelona.

“Yes, yes. It’s clear that in the end I can’t complain about the record I have to this day. Every player wants to win, to win titles, and that’s what we’re here for,” he stated.

Garcia also confirmed that he is due to report back for Barcelona duty on 12 August as preparations continue for the new season.

title: Infantino tells critics to 'meditate, pray' as he hails World Cup
description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has dismissed criticism on the governing body and the World Cup and accused opponents of "spreading hate and false rumours. fullText:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino has dismissed criticism on the governing body and the World Cup and accused opponents of "spreading hate and false rumours."

Infantino said in an lengthy Instagram post early Monday that the tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada was "the most outstanding World Cup" which "celebrated humanity at its best."

He suggested that the critics “take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match” because "our world needs love, not hate; tolerance, not division; celebration, not mourning."

Infantino highlighted the peaceful atmosphere at the 16 venues and that billions from around the world had watched the June 11-July 19 tournament.

"Sorry that the matches are now over and sorry that you missed all that joy and togetherness. Sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all," Infantino told the critics.

He said that while "you spread hatred we worked tirelessly to unite countries at war" and claimed that "Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict."

He did not mention criticism from the Iran team on the visa restrictions imposed on them by US authorities or the entry ban for designated Somali World Cup referee Omar Artan, rather highlighting that millions of others had no visa problems.

Infantino also dismissed criticism on refereeing and disciplinary matters which culminated in the lifting of an automatic red card ban for American player Folarin Balogun after an intervention from US President Donald Trump.

He said it was "curious" that the criticism came from countries where similar practices are "routine and widely accepted."

"Football is about unity, not division. Football is bigger than hate and discrimination," Infantino said in general terms, stating he was "incredibly proud" to have done his share.

title: Aces add another player heading off to FIBA World Cup
description: While the Las Vegas Aces are expected to be heavy contributors to the rosters for the 2026 FIBA World Cup, another lesser-known player is going back to represent her country once again.
fullText:
While the Las Vegas Aces are expected to be heavy contributors to the rosters for the 2026 FIBA World Cup, another lesser-known player is going back to represent her country once again.

On Sunday, it was confirmed that Aces forward Stephanie Talbot would be a part of Team Australia for the World Cup, which is set to go from Sept. 4-13 in Berlin.

It has been something of a challenging season for Talbot in her first go-around in Las Vegas, averaging only 3.5 points and three rebounds per game despite starting all but one of her 26 games and averaging 18.5 minutes.

However, Talbot’s international experience was what drew interest from the Aces, and Australia boasts one of the top women’s basketball teams in the world, with their most recent triumph being a bronze medal at the 2024 Olympics.

More holdovers from that bronze medal team include head coach Sandy Brondello (Toronto Tempo), as well as Isobel Borlase (Atlanta Dream), Ezi Magbegor (Seattle Storm), Jade Melbourne (Seattle), Alanna Smith (Dallas Wings) and Sami Whitcomb (Phoenix Mercury). The team is also confirmed to include another WNBA player in Chloe Bibby (Chicago Sky) to their ranks.

Talbot has been a part of Team Australia since 2015, participating in three Olympics and two World Cups so far. She played a part in the Australians taking home silver medals in the 2018 World Cups and bronze in the 2022 rendition, where she was also named to the All-Star five of the tournament.

Back in somewhat more familiar and friendlier territory, a good tournament could be what Talbot needs to find her footing and gain some momentum when the Aces begin their likely playoff push.

title: Casemiro makes Inter Miami debut despite MLS investigation into transfer
description: Casemiro plays, Messi sits out during his post-World Cup rest, and Suarez scores to give Miami a sixth straight MLS win.
fullText:
Brazilian midfielder Casemiro made his debut for Inter Miami despite an ongoing investigation by Major League Soccer (MLS) into his transfer to the United States club.

The former Manchester United man played the full match as Inter Miami defeated Montreal 1-0 on Saturday. Last week, MLS said it was investigating a “tampering allegation” against the club following Casemiro’s arrival.

The league’s inquiry cast a shadow over the midfielder’s arrival, with MLS saying it would withhold details of a settlement between Inter Miami and LA Galaxy over Casemiro’s “discovery rights” until the review concludes.

Under MLS rules, clubs must negotiate discovery rights with any team that previously listed a player before signing him outside the draft or free agency. The Galaxy had held rights to Casemiro before he opted to join Miami instead.

Miami’s 1-0 win in Canada came courtesy of an 81st-minute Luis Suarez penalty. The spot kick was awarded after German Berterame banged heads with Montreal defender Efrain Morales in the box.

Berterame was knocked unconscious and taken away in an ambulance following the collision.

Inter Miami interim coach Guillermo Hoyos confirmed after the match that Berterame was conscious and “doing well”.

“The blow was very strong, but he is recovering,” Hoyos added.

Suarez sent a soft shot past Sebastian Breza for his ninth goal of the season and his sixth in the last three matches to give Inter Miami their sixth straight victory.

Lionel Messi was rested once again as he continues his recovery following Argentina’s run to the World Cup final.

title: LAFC continues to surge in dominant showing against Sporting KC
description: Los Angeles remained perfect following the World Cup break, doing so in commanding fashion.
fullText:
Perhaps a few weeks of rest were all LAFC really needed to get back on track, with another wire-to-wire victory in the books. This time around, it was a 4-0 shutout performance against Sporting KC on Saturday evening, helping the Black & Gold secure three points for the fourth consecutive match.

Just like in Wednesday's win over Real Salt Lake, it was Son Heung-min and Denis Bouanga combining to provide the necessary fireworks in front of the home crowd. The duo combined for three scores on the night, helping LA set an emphatic tone early on.

It took Son less than five minutes to find the scoresheet, using his speed to get behind the Kansas City defense and meet a promising ball from Mark Delgado before tapping it calmly into the left side of the net.

THREE IN THREE FOR SON HEUNG-MIN!@LAFC lead within five minutes!

📺 Apple TV: https://t.co/QuMdm9OkRD pic.twitter.com/pYLoAqpBew

— Major League Soccer (@MLS) July 26, 2026

The 34-year-old has returned to action following the World Cup looking fresh with motivation, now having scored in each of the squad's three recent matches. LAFC, however, was only just beginning to make its mark on the scoresheet as a whole.

Bouanga had his turn next, using a burst of speed to make it 2-0 in the 37th minute. He followed Mathieu Choinière's lob all the way down the pitch, cleverly tapping it forward with his head and shooting past KC goalkeeper Stefan Cleveland.

Denis Bouanga strikes with lightning speed!

Blink and you might miss @LAFC's second goal. ⚡ pic.twitter.com/Yj3HntEsGZ

— Major League Soccer (@MLS) July 26, 2026

His ninth goal of the season served as the latest example of LAFC's recent effectiveness in transition. David Martínez found a goal of his own before the conclusion of the opening half, getting loose on a run down the pitch of his own and using a stop-and-start move to free himself for a strike from close range.

David Martinez nets @LAFC's third of the half!

The entire front three getting on the scoresheet in the opening 45 minutes. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/rsRSIh8hIc

— Major League Soccer (@MLS) July 26, 2026

Before the night's end, Bouanga ultimately struck once more to pocket a brace and secure double-digit goals on the season. Another long pass, this time from Ryan Porteous, landed at the feet of a running Tyler Boyd on the right side. His well-placed ball back toward Bouanga just inside the center of the box was enough for LA's leading scorer to make it 4-0.

Bouanga Brace!! 🚀@LAFC have scored 4️⃣! pic.twitter.com/V8pC2RIlMo

— Major League Soccer (@MLS) July 26, 2026

With the full-time whistle, LAFC improved to 10-5-3 overall, now tied atop the Western Conference table at 33 points with the Vancouver Whitecaps and San Jose Earthquakes. The Black & Gold also managed to continue their dominant stretch against KC in the process, now having gone unbeaten in their last 10 games against the club.

Since returning to play, LA has now scored 10 goals while conceding just one. Hugo Lloris earned his second clean sheet on Saturday since returning from the break, needing to make just one save.

LAFC will return to action seeking a fifth consecutive victory on Saturday, Aug. 1, heading north of the border to battle the Whitecaps in a clash of Western Conference leaders. The two sides have not squared off since the semifinals of the 2025 MLS Cup Playoffs, where Vancouver emerged victorious in a dramatic penalty shootout.

Kickoff is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT.

title: Bayern Munich among top five clubs to be compensated by FIFA following World Cup
description: A lot of risk, less reward?
fullText:
The relationship between club and international football has always been shaky at best. Clubs fear injuries that could derail an entire season while international teams pine for their nation’s top talents — a complex conflict of interest.

Nowhere is the conflict as prominent as the FIFA World Cup. Clubs have no choice but to surrender their talent to their national teams. The hesitancy isn’t a product of not wanting players to represent their countries on the world’s greatest stage. It is rather a matter of risk.

Already fatigued after a long season of club football, players are at a heightened risk of injury — not to mention the select few who decide to play through afflictions for the pride of representing their country at the World Cup. Germany’s Lennart Karl and Nico Schlotterbeck suffered tournament-ending injuries, while Belgium’s Amadou Onana sustained a torn ACL mid-tournament. Argentinian pair Facundo Medina and Lisandro Martínez both face an extended stint on the sidelines, England’s Tino Livramento picked up a fresh setback in a long line of past injuries, and Morocco’s Abde Ezzalzouli was ruled out for six weeks after injuring his knee.

Among other reasons, to make up for the immense risk FIFA offers compensation for clubs whose players feature at the World Cup.

According to Kicker (via @iMiaSanMia), Bayern Munich is one of the clubs that will benefit the most.

Compensation payments paid out by FIFA to clubs for releasing their players for the World Cup:

1- Manchester City €3.08m
2- PSG €2.49m
3- Arsenal €2.42m
4- Bayern €2.3m
5- Barcelona €2.2m
6- Chelsea €2.12m

Whether the compensation provided by FIFA truly outweighs the extra kilometres players clock and a heightened risk of injury is up for debate. But, the fact that there is compensation — a luxury that didn’t always exist — is a step in the right direction.

fullText:
Lionel Messi will not be required to play in next week's Major League Soccer All-Star Game after representing Argentina in the recent World Cup final, the US domestic league said Saturday.

Inter Miami superstar Messi had been sanctioned last year for skipping the annual showcase, which pits top players from across MLS against rivals from the Mexican Liga-MX.

Participation is usually mandatory, with exceptions for injury.

But this year, the World Cup took place in the middle of the MLS season, which paused for a seven-week break, and the league confirmed exceptions had been pre-arranged for players reaching the international tournament's final stages.

"Prior to the start of the 2026 season, Major League Soccer and the MLS Players Association agreed that upon a player's exit from the World Cup competition, clubs would have individual conversations with each player to determine the appropriate rest and return to training and competition timeline," said the statement.

"Consistent with that agreement, Rodrigo De Paul and Lionel Messi will be excused from participating in the 2026 MLS All-Star Game."

Fellow Argentine De Paul also featured in last Sunday's World Cup final in New Jersey, which Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time.

Messi had been among the first 11 players named to the MLS squad for this year's All-Star Game, which takes place in Charlotte, North Carolina, on Wednesday.

In his absence, stars will include Los Angeles FC's Son Heung-min, the Vancouver Whitecaps' Thomas Muller, and US national team captain Tim Ream, who plays for Charlotte.

Last year, Messi and then-Inter Miami teammate Jordi Alba were slapped with a one-game suspension for skipping the All-Star Game at the last minute.

MLS commissioner Don Garber at the time expressed sympathy for Messi's grueling schedule, saying it had been a "very difficult decision" and that the league's long-standing All-Star Game policy would be reviewed.

fullText:
The World Cup may be over, but soccer continues to draw strong viewership. A USL Championship match following the World Cup recorded the second-highest TV audience in USL history.

The Pittsburgh Riverhounds-Louisville City FC match on July 18 averaged 453,000 viewers. That is the second-highest recorded audience in USL history. The 2024 USL Championship Final averaged 606,000 viewers on CBS.

Viewership for Pittsburgh-Louisville was only slightly lower than MLS in primetime on Fox the day before. Nashville-Atlanta averaged 587,000 viewers on Fox. However, unlike the USL, MLS airs all of its games on streaming via Apple TV, meaning it’s unclear how many additional viewers watched on the streamer.

The USL, which operates below MLS in the U.S. soccer pyramid, is attempting to compete with the higher-level league. Its newest media rights deal includes over-the-air exposure on CBS and cable broadcasts on ESPN and CBS Sports Network. MLS has an over-the-air deal with Fox, but the network is not scheduled to air another MLS game until the MLS Cup.

In 2028, the USL plans to launch “USL Premier,” which would compete directly with MLS. Unlike MLS, however, USL Premier is scheduled to feature promotion and relegation from the USL Championship.

The USL Championship still has a way to go to compete with MLS fully. The 2025 MLS Cup averaged 994,000 viewers on Fox and Fox Deportes, which is more than any USL matchup on television. Viewership for the MLS Cup again does not include viewership on Apple TV.

But if this latest viewership mark is any indication, there appears to be momentum for the USL following the World Cup. If the USL wants to compete with MLS one day truly, it will need to continue building on this viewership success.

Now it has been reported that Real Madrid do indeed hope to sign Manchester City’s midfield general this summer. All of a sudden, a summer defining moment has landed at Manchester City’s doorstep.

It is also reported that as yet no direct talks have taken place between Manchester City and Real Madrid over a deal for Rodri. It is also included in The Athletic report that Manchester City are hopeful that Rodri will see out the final year of his contract. However, Rodri has previously expressed his wish to return to Spain and now Real Madrid are determined to make Rodri’s wish come true this summer.

A fork in the moment has arrived for Manchester City in the summer transfer window. David Ornstein and Mario Cortegana’s report illustrates that Real Madrid do indeed want to sign Rodri this summer. Rodri’s wish to one day play for the La Liga giants is by now well-established. City now have a decision to make assuming that Real Madrid can satisfy City’s asking price to sell the World Cup winner.

Does Manchester City hold Rodri to the final year of his contract? Rodri remains Manchester City’s most important player. A fully fit Rodri turns City from a very good side into an elite side. Selling Rodri would create a sizable void in Manchester City’s midfield and in their leadership. Is that something City are willing to allow to occur? That answer isn’t immediately clear but the fact that Rodri is so important to City may provide that particular answer.

The other side to the coin is whether Manchester City keeps a player who clearly wants to leave the club. Typically, besides Bernardo Silva, City do not keep players who wish to leave. Perhaps Rodri’s time at City has naturally concluded as he has nothing left to achieve at the club. He has scaled every mountain.

Do the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders want to keep player, no matter how important they are, who doesn’t want to be there? The answer to that particular question, has the potential to massively alter City’s summer transfer window plans.

Manchester City have seemingly reached a defining moment this summer. Rodri remains Manchester City’s most important player. Real Madrid now want to sign him, and he wants a move back to Spain. Whatever City decides to do with Rodri will define their summer. It is that big, and hopefully a decision one way or another comes quickly so City can plan for what lies ahead with or without Rodri.

title: Rodri to have back surgery but Maresca brushes off transfer speculation
description: World Cup winner Rodri is to have back surgery, says new Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca.
fullText:
World Cup winner Rodri will have surgery on a back issue on Monday, new Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has confirmed.

The 30-year-old Spain captain guided his country to World Cup glory last week and was named the Golden Ball winner as player of the tournament.

But the midfielder's last two seasons at club level were heavily disrupted - an anterior cruciate ligament injury leaving him sidelined for the majority of the 2024-25 campaign before several setbacks last season meant he was often unavailable.

The Ballon d'Or winner was back to his best at the World Cup but, speaking at his first news conference since being appointed City boss, Maresca said Rodri now needs surgery followed by recuperation.

"Now, [he has] surgery on Monday. Then he needs a holiday, he needs to rest and recover and then he will be back with us," the Italian coach said.

Maresca did not elaborate on when Rodri might return though he did dismiss speculation around the Spaniard's future at Etihad Stadium following reports in the past week linking him with a move to Real Madrid.

"Around big players there are always speculations so I am not worried about that," he said.

"I think it is normal, also because they [Spain] won the World Cup and because he is one of the best players. I think every manager wants to have Rodri because he is a top player."

Of other players still to return, Maresca said he expected to have them in the squad three or four days before City face Premier League champions Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday, 16 August.

Why Maresca? What Man City fans can expect from Guardiola's successor

Rodri's stock at all-time high as he adds to trophy collection

In his first news conference since succeeding Pep Guardiola last month, Maresca found himself fielding questions about the Catalan, who won 20 trophies in his 10 years at the club.

The 46-year-old knows only too well the tough act he has to follow having worked as Guardiola's assistant during the 2022-23 Treble-winning season.

"I want to say it is a privilege because it's the reason why the club decided to go for me, that is a privilege," he said.

"I have said many times, I consider Pep the best coach in the world in the last 20-25 years. It is a challenge [to replace him]."

Maresca, who called time on his time at Chelsea in January after 18 months, acknowledged the challenge of arriving at a club who have had just three managers in 16 years.

"That is not normal and has not happened often," he said. "I am confident that we can continue to do a great job and continue to do the job that has been done in the last 14, 15 years since Roberto Mancini was here.

"I know the organisation quite well and the people inside the club from years ago. The structure understands to give time for everything.

"Since Manchester City contacted me, I had no doubt about joining this fantastic club."

Maresca hinted that there were "a few things to do" in the transfer window but would not be drawn on the futures of players including goalkeeper James Trafford, who has been linked with a move away from the club, and returning midfielder Jack Grealish, who spent last season on loan at Everton but is back in training with City.

title: Tyler Adams Explains Mauricio Pochettino’s Impact on USMNT

fullText:
The biggest news that fans of the United States Men’s National Team are waiting for is the decision by current head coach Mauricio Pochettino. Will he accept the contract extension that U.S. Soccer offered before the start of the World Cup? That’s the question that U.S. Soccer hopes will be answered soon.

Midfielder Tyler Adams spoke with Stars & Stripes FC this week as part of his work with Allstate opening up a mini-pitch in Atlanta. He took the time during that interview to explain the impact Pochettino had on him and the rest of the USMNT.

“I’ve been very fortunate with the managers I’ve been able to work under and learn from. [How] Pochettino leads a group of people and the culture he leads with is so important,” Adams said. “Put the tactics and how he improved me as a player aside, how he improved me as a person, the intangibles and the culture he created was incredible.”

Pochettino led the USMNT to the Round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup, setting a record for most USMNT wins at a single World Cup in the process. Since he took over as head coach in September 2024, he has a 17W-12L-2D record. During the World Cup, he had the team competing at their highest ability until it all fell apart in the Round of 16 against Belgium. Still, having a full cycle of Pochettino, despite the history with coaches getting a second cycle, could bring some continuity that the team hasn’t had in quite some time.

Pochettino has said that a decision on his future will come soon. Should he continue as coach, it seems like he will have a player pool that will fight for him as they attempt to build on the foundation they’ve set and keep fans engaged and supportive. The 28-year-old midfielder's contract was running down as he joined the Australia squad just three days after being "devastated" by the final-day loss to Celtic that meant Heart of Midlothian were pipped to the Scottish title by their hosts.

Devlin was weighing up whether to accept a new deal from the Edinburgh club amid rival interest, before Derek McInnes' own switch from Hearts to become Rangers manager decided the midfielder's destiny.

"It was devastating, but I didn't have much time to reflect on how last season ended and then straight into the World Cup, which is one of the most special moments of your career.

"I thought it would be a good idea going there off-contract, but it wasn't.
